User test (playtest done with an AI agent for TidyMaze):
What was tested: the three leagues. In each one I wrote a bot that uses only the ready-made moves (STANCE, GUARD, OVERHAND, STEP_FORWARD, WAIT) and played games against the default AI in the demo IDE: 3 games in league 1, 3 in league 2 and 6 in league 3 (two bot versions). JOINTS and stamina were not used by my bot, so I have no play evidence for them.
Rules I checked: the damage formula in the statement (zone x (closing speed - 2), rounded) matched all 101 head and torso hits with a speed in the summaries of the saved games, and every fall that cost HP was 20 HP. A fall right after a push, with no HP lost, was reported as the statement says.
Unclear or missing: the text for JOINTS (league 2) and stamina (league 3) was read but not tested.
Good: the per-turn summary lines, with the closing speed and the HP lost, make it easy to see why a fight was won or lost.

Thanks a lot for the kind words about the viewer!

Yes, I'm looking into it. Since you can control each of your fighter's 15 joints, the input describes both bodies in full: 19 points and 15 joints per fighter, which makes 68 of the 72 lines. I was so focused on the physics (balance, creating your own moves, lots of room for creativity) that I didn't think about the size of the input, and I had missed the stub best practices. 

When I saw 5DN1L's comment, my first reaction was: oops! 😅

I'm now looking into a lighter input, or maybe a change in the game mechanics.

The viewer is brilliant, but 72 lines of input seems a bit much to me. Not sure if it can be simplified, though :O
Upvoted for the work!

I haven't read the statement in detail or done any play-testing yet, but the official best practises state that:

> The number of variables per loop should not exceed 10.

https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/creating-your-own-puzzle

I'm not sure whether there's any bot game on CG that requires reading 72 lines of input per turn 😅

I've updated the contribution with a lighter input, and the game mechanics stay the same. The input is now 4 lines per turn: one line per fighter, one line with the 38 body points (8 values each) and one line with two counters. A simple bot only needs the two fighter lines and the x of the two pelvises, and the statement shows where to find them.

User test follow-up (playtest done with an AI agent for TidyMaze):
- Stamina table (league 3): the table gives the stamina won or spent "with full stamina and no hit", and JUMP is listed as "+1.13 %". The statement also says a fighter "starts with 100 %, and never has more". At 100 % a gain cannot show, so the table cannot be checked from full stamina. Please say how it should be checked (replay: https://www.codingame.com/replay/921786266).

The table could not be checked from full stamina, and the statement was wrong there. Stamina never goes over 100 %, and what a turn would add above it is lost: from 100 %, a move that gains stamina shows less, or nothing. The values of the table hold when no hit lands and the move starts at 98 % or less.

Your replay shows exactly this. Your JUMP on turn 136 starts at 100 %: its first 4 turns cost 0.96 %, its 5th turn would add 1.37 % but stops at 100 %, and its last 2 turns add nothing, so it ends at 100 %. Your HIGH_KICK on turn 80 also starts at 100 %: the small gains of its first 5 turns are lost, so it costs 1.60 % instead of 1.00 %. Everything else in your replay matches the table once the 100 % cap is taken into account, except STEP_FORWARD (turn 102): a hit on turn 107 takes 10 % of stamina during it.

To check one: hold GUARD for 3 turns (−0.40 % each, so stamina reads 98800), then play the move to its end with no hit. For example JUMP, then WAIT for 6 turns: stamina then reads 99928, that is +1.13 %.

I've updated the statement: the table now says "when no hit lands and the move starts at 98 % or less", with a line under it about the 100 % cap. Note that the same update also changes the input: it is now 4 lines per turn instead of 72, so a bot written before the update has to read it differently.
